subject: Post-call: token velocity & spend runway — pilot economics and open gaps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lewis <emma@acme-pay.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme-pay.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: token velocity & spend runway — pilot economics and open gaps

Emma — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a few concrete asks so we can size the pilot to fit your budget window.

Call summary (high level)
- Primary pain: unpredictable token spend on high-concurrency user flows (chat + document enrichment). Topline: heavy tail of long sessions (~12% of sessions produce 60% of tokens).
- Goal: ship a 6–8 week pilot that validates latency/quality and demonstrates a 30–50% reduction in token spend via batching + prefix caching while keeping user-facing latency under 250ms P95.
- Constraints: procurement wants a constrained pilot (< $15k/month preferred) and SOC2 evidence for evaluation; quarter-end procurement approvals on Aug 10.

Initial economics & levers we discussed
- Token velocity reduction: optimistic ~45% with 200–500ms batching window + prefix/KV caching on repeated prompts; conservative ~25% if personalization prevents prefix reuse.
- Batching trade: 200ms window reduces tokens per second cost but can add ~20–40ms median latency depending on load shape — we can tune for P95.
- Cache hit assumptions: we used a 40% hit-rate baseline for the call demo; we can run a lightweight telemetry sample to validate immediately.

Next steps (asks from us):
1) Confirm the monthly pilot budget cap you want us to target (you mentioned ~$15k).
2) Share a small sample of anonymized session lengths / token counts (one week preferred) so we can run a quick hit-rate simulation.
3) Decision-call: 30-minute sync with procurement + engineering next Tue or Wed to lock scope and contract terms.

Attached: redwood-pilot-estimate.xlsx (simple cost model with three pilot options + ROI waterfall). I’ll follow up with a concise options email with pricing bands.

Thanks —
Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Dylan — really helpful summary, thanks. A few clarifications from procurement and product: 

- Budget: procurement is pushing hard for an initial pilot <= $15,000/mo, ideally structured as a month-to-month with the ability to pause if results don’t meet the ROI thresholds. Can you give a concrete example (numbers) that ends up < $15k/mo?
- Decision timeline: we’re trying to get the pilot signed off before our internal budget review on Aug 10.
- Security: SOC2 Type II report must be available to legal to look over; will that be possible during pilot?

Also: product asked whether batch windows of 200–500ms will noticeably change user experience for our fraud-ops chat flow. If you have any measured examples from similar customers (latency P50/P95 impact), that would help our PMs sign off.

If it helps, we can do the procurement + engineering sync on Wed 21 (10:00am PT).

—Emma

Emma — thanks, I’ll be brief with concrete options so procurement can evaluate quickly: 

Option 1 — Hosted quickstart (no commit)
- Estimated run-rate: $13k/month (based on your session profile projection)
- Assumptions: 40% cache hit; 200ms batching window; 95th % latency target ~220–270ms; measured example: similar payments customer saw P95 increase of ~35ms with 200ms batch window under steady load.

Option 2 — Reserved pilot (1-month reserved capacity)
- Estimated run-rate: $9k/month + $2k one-time setup (net ~$11k first month)
- Assumptions: dedicating a small pool yields more aggressive batching (higher effective batching without spikes) and slightly better unit economics; requires a short purchase order.

Option 3 — Minimum viable scoped pilot (feature-limited)
- Estimated run-rate: ~$7k/mo (limited endpoints, stricter token caps)
- Trade: less production-like traffic, but easier to sign quickly.

Key notes: all options include access to our SOC2 evidence under NDA, token-level billing, and a preflight telemetry run we’ll do free of charge to validate cache-hit assumptions. I attached a one-page breakdown: pilot-option-breakdown.pdf.

Ask: which option maps best to procurement’s comfort level? If Wed 21 @10am PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include a short decision checklist for procurement (max monthly spend, cancellation terms, SLAs needed).

Thanks —
Dylan
Attachment: pilot-option-breakdown.pdf (pdf)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding the AcmePay thread. Quick ask for pricing approval and SOC2 access:

- AcmePay procurement wants a month-to-month pilot <= $15k/mo; product is sensitive to P95 latency but open to a 200ms batching window if we can show ~40ms median impact and keep P95 < 300ms.
- They asked for SOC2 Type II evidence to be shared with legal during evaluation (we typically provide under an NDA).
- They prefer Option 1 or Option 2 from my note; Option 2 would require a short PO.

Requested next steps from you:
1) Approve a price band we can commit to live in-thread for procurement (i.e., authorize up to 20% discount on list for a 1-month reserved pilot).
2) Confirm standard NDA template or one-off for SOC2 sharing.
3) If price ok, I’ll lock the Wed 21 meeting and include an econ slide for procurement.

If it helps, I can also tighten the Option 1 estimate to a hard $ figure (based on their weekly telemetry sample) — happy to pull that if we get approval to run the sample.

—Dylan
